global.tone: No-fluff newspaper briefs: fact first, concrete detail, no hype, no filler.

sections.label: World
sections.prompt: Favor geopolitics and economic policy over local/domestic stories. India's own news runs in The Nation; an India story belongs here only when it is about India abroad (diplomacy, trade, conflict).

sections.label: India
sections.prompt: India's national news from the India pool and the day's leading India stories: central government decisions and policy, the courts, Parliament's work, the economy and jobs, infrastructure and transport, security, disasters and major incidents. Lead with what a well-informed person in India would be embarrassed to miss (high outlets and lead). Skip party politics and campaign speeches, stories that are really about one city (they belong in the city section) and market moves (they belong in the markets section).

sections.label: Markets & Economy
sections.prompt: Mostly Indian markets: Nifty/Sensex moves, RBI policy, the rupee, the Indian economy and SWP/mutual fund news — about three of every five stories. Fill the rest with global markets that move India: Wall Street, the Fed, oil, China and big global economic data. Skip pure stock-tip articles.

sections.label: Two Cities
sections.prompt: What changes daily life in the city: civic decisions, metro and roads, water and power, rain alerts, schools, hospitals, jobs and local business. Serious crime only. Skip viral social-media anecdotes and party politics.

sections.label: Technology
sections.prompt: Prefer product launches, AI research and big platform moves over listicles and deals.
